handoff.summary: Batch b10: mortality-rate r2 with the Table 45.1 first-row value as a third published reference.

assumptions: source assumption: columns B (deaths), C (survivors at interval start) and D (mortality per 1000) of a cohort life table such as Table 45.1 (Dall mountain sheep, adapted from Deevey 1947).
source assumption: the rate is normalized per 1000 alive at the interval start (source: 'multiplied by 1000 to get the mortality rate per thousand').

gaps: Quantity meanings death_count, survivors_count and mortality_rate_per_1000 are not in the runtime vocabulary snapshot; runtime projection omitted.

models.inverse_notes: Survivors are recoverable as S = D*1000/q for nonzero q. Substitution check with the rounded published rate: 12*1000/15.5 = 774.2, within the rounding band of the true 776; exact recovery needs the unrounded rate. D = 0 gives q = 0 (no deaths in the interval), which is admissible.
limitations: Applies to one stated age interval of one cohort table; it is not an annualized hazard and must not be compared across different interval lengths without rescaling.
The published values are rounded to one decimal, so recomputation from D and S differs by up to half a table unit.

references.method: Published worked example: 12/776 x 1000 reported as approximately 15.5; exact recomputation gives 15.464, so the 0.05 tolerance covers the source rounding (difference 0.036).
references.provenance: Published result (worked example) kept at the source-reported rounded value with documented rounding propagation.

references.method: Published Table 45.1 row (ages 0.5-1): 145/946 x 1000 reported as 153.3; exact recomputation gives 153.274 (difference 0.026, within tolerance).
references.provenance: Published table value kept at the source-reported rounded value with documented rounding propagation.

references.method: Published Table 45.1 first row (ages 0-0.5): 54 deaths of 1000 give 54/1000 x 1000 = 54.0 per thousand, exact.
references.provenance: Published result (life-table row value) matched by exact integer arithmetic.

rejection_cases.reason: Deaths in the interval (800) cannot exceed survivors at its start (776).
Survivors-at-start S is required; deaths alone do not determine the rate.

relationship.locator: Section 45.1 'Life Tables': formula 'mortality rate = number of individuals dying / number of individuals surviving x 1000' with worked example 12/776 x 1000 approx 15.5 and Table 45.1 (Deevey 1947 sheep data).
relationship.original_equation: mortality rate = number of individuals dying / number of individuals surviving x 1000
relationship.translation_notes: Source column labels mapped to local D (dying, column B) and S (surviving at interval start, column C). The factor 1000 is an exact normalization constant printed in the source, kept inline with this note rather than as a fitted parameter. Dimensional check: count over count is dimensionless; the per-1000 normalization is carried by the unit.

sources.evidence: Paraphrase: mortality rate per 1000 equals deaths during the interval over survivors at its start times 1000; sheep example 12/776 x 1000 approx 15.5; Table 45.1 rows such as 145/946 -> 153.3.
